title: Annotatio IV §.IV: First argument — OT spiritual food and drink; the Rock was Christ
pass_a_gloss: The first is taken from the Communion and participation of Christ — and so of Christ’s body and blood (without which Christ is not even Christ) — imparted to Old Testament Christians, of whom the Apostle at v. 1 does not want us ignorant that all ate the same spiritual food and drank the same spiritual drink, not only among themselves but with us; For it immediately follows: For they drank of the spiritual Rock that followed; and the Rock was Christ; But of this alone we New Testament Christians also drink His blood spiritually, as also the spiritual food, the Manna descending from heaven, i.e. Christ and His body, and nothing else, participating likewise with the Fathers of the Old Testament, the sacraments of the ancients differing from ours as to Signs, but the same as to Signifieds — Augustine Tract. 26 on John, following Peter: But we believe that through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they. (Acts 15:11).
pass_b_english: First argument: OT believers already shared Christ’s communion — the same spiritual food and drink (1 Cor. 10:1–4); the Rock was Christ.
We NT Christians drink His blood spiritually and share the same spiritual food — Christ and His body — with the Fathers; signs differ, significata are the same (Augustine; Acts 15:11).
source_text: Primum desumtum à Communione & participatione Christi, eòque corporis & sanguinis Christi (quibus sine Christus ne Christus quidem est) Veteris Testamenti Christianis impertita, de quibus Apostolus versu 1. Non vult nos ignorare, omnes eandem escam spiritualem edisse, omnes item eundem potum spiritualem bibisse, puta non inter se tantum omnes, sed & nobiscum; Nam immediatè sequitur: Bibebant enim ex sequenti spirituali Petra; Petra verò erat Christus; Sed de hoc solo & nosmet Christiani N. T., sanguinem ejus spiritualiter bibimus, sicuti & escam spiritualem, Mannam de cœlo descendentem, i. e. Christum ejusque corpus, nec quicquam aliud, itidem cum Patribus V. Test. participamus, Sacramentis Veterum, quoad Signa quidem, à nostris, diversis, quoad Significata verò iisdem existentibus, dicente Augustino Tract. 26. super Johannem, juxta istud Petrinum: Quin verò, per Gratiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi, credimus nos Salvatum iri, kath' hon tropon kakeinoi. Act. 15, 11.
